**Odense: Børne- og Ungdomspsykiatrisk Ambulatorium** (Odense Child and Adolescent Psychiatric Outpatient Clinic) is a psychiatric facility operating within [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] in Denmark. In the context of the national ADHD-Databasen annual reports for 2023 and 2024, the clinic stands out as a rare example of high-quality diagnostic practice amidst a broader systemic crisis where most national process indicators fall far below the 90% standard.

The facility is particularly notable for its performance on [[indikator-1|Indikator 1]], which measures the completion of somatic assessments during ADHD evaluations. While the national average struggles, Odense achieved an 89% fulfillment rate (95% CI: 84–93) for the period of April 1, 2023, to March 31, 2024, making it one of the few facilities approaching the standard [^src1]. This performance reflects a stable, high-quality trend, with the clinic scoring 92% in 2022/23 and 82% in 2021/22 [^src1]. 

Furthermore, the clinic excels in age-specific diagnostic indicators. For [[indikator-2a|Indikator 2a]] (clinical environmental observation for children aged 0–5), the facility met the standard, achieving a 100% fulfillment rate [^src6]. For [[indikator-2b|Indikator 2b]] (structured diagnostic interview or environmental observation for children aged 6–17), Odense reported a 98% fulfillment rate across 174 assessment courses, distinguishing it as the only department in the country to fully meet the standard for this metric [^src4]. Other data points from the 2023/24 reporting period confirm this exceptional performance, showing a 98% fulfillment rate (95% CI: 95–100) [^src7] and a 94% rate in another dataset [^src3].

Despite these diagnostic successes, the clinic faces the same systemic challenges as the rest of the country regarding post-diagnostic coordination. For Indicator 4, which tracks coordinating network meetings within 90 days, the clinic achieved a 64% fulfillment rate [^src5]. While this falls short of the 90% national standard, it represents the highest performance among all departments handling more than 10 assessment courses, highlighting the severe structural barriers in cross-sectoral collaboration across Danish child and adolescent psychiatry [^src5].
